exr:i01-01: Use distributivity on \(a(v+(-v))\) and identify the additive inverse of \(av\).
exr:i01-03: Use pointwise addition and scalar multiplication, then check that continuity is preserved by both operations.
exr:i01-04: Check whether the zero vector belongs to the set; scalar closure gives a second quick test.
exr:i01-05: Ask which scalars are available. Over \(\mathbb C\), \(1\) suffices; over \(\mathbb R\), separate real and imaginary parts.
exr:i01-07: Check the vector-space axioms entrywise; identify the zero matrix and additive inverses.
exr:i01-08: Use associativity repeatedly; a short induction on the number of summands formalizes the argument.
exr:i03-02: Solve \(a(1,0)+b(1,1)=(3,2)\) directly; the coefficients you obtain are the coordinates.
exr:i03-05: A basis of \(U\) is an independent list in \(V\) with \(\dim V\) vectors; use the dimension bound for independent lists.
exr:i04-06: Track only how the coordinate entries are reordered, and test the rule on basis coordinate vectors.
exr:i04-07: Keep the abstract vector fixed and compare only its coordinate columns in two different bases.
exr:i04-08: Use the explicit inverse for a nearly parallel basis and observe the entries of size \(1/\varepsilon\).
exr:i05-02: Test the zero vector first: a linear map must send \(0\) to \(0\).
exr:i05-05: Write an arbitrary vector as a linear combination of the basis and use linearity of both maps.
exr:i05-06: Try a coordinate shift such as \(N(x,y)=(y,0)\) and compute \(N^2\).
exr:i05-07: Define addition and scalar multiplication pointwise on maps and verify the vector-space axioms.
exr:i06-01: Set \(T(x,y,z)=0\) and solve the resulting homogeneous equations.
exr:i06-02: Use rank--nullity after computing the kernel dimension in the preceding exercise.
exr:i06-03: If \(T(v)=T(w)\), apply linearity to \(v-w\); for the converse compare \(T(v)\) with \(T(0)\).
exr:i06-04: Surjectivity means \(\operatorname{im}T=W\); compare the dimensions of these spaces.
exr:i06-05: Extend a basis of \(U\) to a basis of \(V\) and inspect the cosets of the added basis vectors.
exr:i07-02: The coordinate vector of the \(j\)-th domain basis vector is \(e_j\); multiplying by the matrix selects column \(j\).
exr:i07-04: Identify one nonzero column and show that every other column is a scalar multiple of it.
exr:i07-06: Apply the reflection to \(e_1\) and \(e_2\); those two images are the matrix columns.
exr:i07-07: Use explicit transformations whose compositions depend on order, such as a projection and a rotation.
exr:i08-04: For a diagonal matrix, only the identity permutation contributes to the determinant.
exr:i08-05: Use cyclicity \(\operatorname{tr}(XY)=\operatorname{tr}(YX)\) with a factorization that places \(P^{-1}P\) together.
exr:i08-06: Choose a basis consisting of one normal direction and a basis of the reflecting hyperplane, then read the diagonal matrix.
exr:i08-07: Write the diagonal entries of \(uv^T\) explicitly and add them.
exr:i08-08: Two matrices of the same endomorphism in different bases are similar; use multiplicativity of determinant and cyclicity of trace.
exr:i09-03: If the zero vector were allowed, it would satisfy \(T0=\lambda0\) for every scalar \(\lambda\); explain why that carries no spectral information.
exr:i09-04: Use \(E_\lambda=\ker(T-\lambda I)\) and the fact that kernels of linear maps are subspaces.
exr:i09-05: Compare the roots of the same characteristic polynomial over \(\mathbb R\) and over \(\mathbb C\).
exr:i10-01: If \(v\in E_\lambda\), compute \(T(v)\) and check that it remains in the same eigenspace.
exr:i10-04: For a diagonal operator, try the span of any subset of eigenbasis vectors.
exr:i10-05: A real triangular matrix has real diagonal eigenvalues; compare this with a real rotation having no real eigenvalue.
exr:i10-06: The matrix \(tI-A\) is triangular; take the product of its diagonal entries.
exr:i11-04: Use \(V=\operatorname{im}P\oplus\ker P\) and determine how \(P\) acts on each summand.
exr:i11-07: Use the Lagrange polynomial that is \(1\) at \(\lambda_i\) and \(0\) at every other eigenvalue.
exr:i13-03: A vector \((a,b)\) is orthogonal to every vector on the \(x\)-axis exactly when its first coordinate is zero.
exr:i13-04: Expand both squared norms and cancel the cross terms.
exr:i14-05: In reduced QR with full column rank, \(Q\) has one orthonormal column for each column of \(A\), while \(R\) is square \(n\times n\).
exr:i15-02: Take determinants in \(Q^TQ=I\) and use \(\det(Q^T)=\det Q\).
exr:i15-04: Apply the unitary operator to an orthonormal basis and use inner-product preservation.
exr:i15-05: Use \(Q^{-1}=Q^*\), then compute the adjoint of \(Q^{-1}\).
exr:i15-06: A diagonal matrix with one \(-1\) and the remaining diagonal entries \(1\) gives an immediate example.
exr:i16-01: For \(Tv=\lambda v\), compare \(\langle Tv,v\rangle\) with \(\langle v,Tv\rangle\) using the stated complex convention.
exr:i16-02: Find the two eigenspaces, normalize one vector in each, and use them as columns of an orthogonal matrix.
exr:i16-04: Apply positivity to an eigenvector: \(\langle Tv,v\rangle=\lambda\|v\|^2\).
exr:i16-06: For \(w\in U^\perp\) and \(u\in U\), rewrite \(\langle Tw,u\rangle\) using self-adjointness.
exr:i17-02: Expand \(q(u+v)\) using bilinearity and symmetry, then solve for \(B(u,v)\).
exr:i17-03: Substitute \(x=Py\) into \(x^TAx\) and collect the two factors of \(P\).
exr:i17-06: If \(Av=0\) for a nonzero vector \(v\), evaluate \(v^TAv\).
exr:i17-07: Use the orthogonal variables \(u=(x+y)/\sqrt2\), \(v=(x-y)/\sqrt2\), then solve for \(x,y\).
exr:i18-01: Compute \(A^*A\); the singular values are the nonnegative square roots of its eigenvalues.
exr:i18-03: One inclusion is immediate; for the converse use \(\langle A^*Av,v\rangle=\|Av\|^2\).
exr:i18-05: Reciprocate only the positive diagonal singular values and transpose the rectangular shape.
exr:i18-06: Diagonalization requires an endomorphism; SVD instead uses orthonormal bases in the domain and codomain separately.
